drills.q: Find all bridges in an undirected network (Critical Connections in a Network, LC 1192). State the exact bridge condition.
drills.a: Single DFS with discovery time and low-link; tree edge (u,v) is a bridge iff low[v] > disc[u] (strict inequality), excluding the parent edge when checking back edges.

drills.q: Find all articulation points in an undirected network, including the root's special-case rule.
drills.a: Non-root u is an articulation point if some child v has low[v] >= disc[u]. The DFS root is a special case: articulation point iff it has more than one DFS-tree child.

drills.q: Implement Tarjan's SCC algorithm. What is the exact condition for a vertex being an SCC root, and why does the on_stack check matter (not just visited)?
drills.a: low[v] == disc[v] means the vertex is an SCC root. A vertex can be visited (disc != -1) but already popped into a previously-finished SCC (not on_stack) -- treating it as still 'in progress' if you only check visited would incorrectly merge separate SCCs.

drills.q: Given boolean clauses each with exactly two literals, determine satisfiability using 2-SAT. Build the implication graph for clause (a OR b) and state the unsatisfiability check.
drills.a: Add edges NOT a -> b and NOT b -> a. Compute SCCs of the implication graph; the formula is unsatisfiable iff some variable x and NOT x are in the same SCC (mutual implication is a direct contradiction).

drills.q: Prove why the condensation graph formed by collapsing each SCC to a single node is always a DAG.
drills.a: If distinct SCCs formed a cycle in the condensation, every vertex in every SCC on that cycle could reach every other vertex in every other SCC by chaining through the cycle -- meaning they were all mutually reachable and should have been one single SCC, contradicting the maximality of the SCC decomposition.

drills.q: Design a build system that detects groups of mutually-dependent modules that must compile together, then produces a valid build order for the resulting groups.
drills.a: Model modules and dependencies as a directed graph, compute SCCs (each is a maximal group of mutually-dependent modules), condense into a DAG (collapsing each SCC to one node, keeping inter-SCC edges), then topologically sort the condensation for a valid build order.
